summary: After Horace's death, PKD buys a four-drawer fireproof file case (700 lbs) and spends days archiving his Unknown and Astounding magazine collection (1933–1943), photographs, letters, manuscripts, and rare Bruno Walter Magic Flute recording.
PKD attends a 'well people' group-therapy session 8pm to 1:30am, with a psychiatrist guiding interpersonal mechanism analysis; Nancy now also attends.
PKD writes a script for the ABC TV show The Invaders, hopeful Quinn Martin Productions will buy it.
PKD's COUNTER-CLOCK WORLD is published by Berkley Books; PKD notes the cover-art girl resembles Nancy and the protagonist Lotta is modeled on her.
PKD's beloved cat Horace dies the prior week, evidently from rat-poison ingestion; PKD records it as a foundational loss two years into ownership.
Nancy Hackett (PKD's fourth wife) is approximately one week away from giving birth to their daughter Isa; PKD has logistical plans (cashier's check for $200, cab fare envelope) for the hospital.
PKD's second cat Johnny disappears after Horace's death and is presumed to have been adopted by another family; PKD's I-Ching consultation reports 'his feet are tied' and 'tender meat'.
PKD starts a new novel, completes 16 pages, then hits writer's block; blames the new baby Isa and wife Nancy for the disruption.
Participates in Berkeley and Marin counterculture social circles during late sixties
